verdict.tagline: Dark, unforgiving cooperative shooter demanding absolute coordination over casual fun.
for_you_if: you have a dedicated squad of tactical players
you thrive on brutal difficulty and stealth

GTFO is a hardcore cooperative first-person shooter built around stealth, coordination, and high difficulty PvE missions. Players take on the role of prisoners forced into underground complex expeditions where resource scarcity, sound management, and synchronized team execution are essential for survival.

GTFO is experienced almost exclusively as a session-based co-op tactical game. Its structure is organized into “expeditions” that function like handcrafted scenarios rather than open-ended systems or live-service progression loops. The game’s longevity comes from its challenging mission design and the need for consistent team coordination, often with dedicated groups rather than random matchmaking.

Its strengths are intense atmosphere, strong sound design, and deeply demanding cooperative mechanics that reward communication and planning. However, it has a very steep learning curve, minimal accessibility for solo or casual play, and a pacing style that can feel punishing or slow compared to mainstream shooters.

Overall, GTFO is best understood as a high-difficulty cooperative survival shooter. It prioritizes coordination and tension over accessibility, making it a niche but highly distinctive experience for dedicated co-op groups.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe companion bots as unhelpful and lacking critical thinking, particularly during stealth sections.

citations.review_text:
Great atmosphere, good sound effects.

Other than those two aspects, the rest of the game is not fun.
First of all, the difficulty spike in this game is abysmal. The early levels are pretty whatever, but definitely doable. Later levels become legitimately near impossible and practically unfun because of the sheer amount of enemies.
The guns and gadgets you can give your person are majority useless, as a lot of them either do too little damage, have too little ammo, or suffer both issues. There is a meta in this game that you basically must have to run.
Early levels can be fun because you can mix and match going stealthy and striking sleepers (the common enemy) in the head with your sledgehammer, or rushing a room and either still using your melee or using a gun, blast them to high hell. Later levels are strictly stealth only unless you have to do a holdout. Engaging in combat in the higher levels is such a pain because there are way too many enemies that do a ton of damage, and ammo is SCARCE. Beginner levels suffer from a lack of ammo, so imagine what later levels are.
Mess ups at higher difficulties are 99 percent unrecoverable, so you basically have to do everything with near maximum efficiency.
Bots are practically useless because, like all bots, they lack critical thinking. Despite being able to direct your bots to go do something for you by using a variety of commands, they don't get the job done like another person would, leading to my next point.
PLAY WITH PEOPLE. Solo sucks, multiplayer is infinitely better. It is the only way to make meaningful progress in this game.
If you wish, buy this game when it's on sale, try it out and make sure you don't exceed 3 hours (so that way you are still eligible for a refund), because this game does not fit everyone's playstyle.

Pros: Fun gameplay, fun stealth mechanics, unique world and story, fantastic co-op and a fairly short learning curve if you're familiar with FPS games, great enemy design and weaknesses, challenging, rewarding when accomplished, some dialogue options really humanize the squad in a fun way I haven't seen before; visually disconcerting with zerg-rush horror.
Cons: AI is completely re tard ed, the end-of-game run is arbitrarily hard and terrible to push through with minimal ammo and medical supplies remaining, lack of materials makes stealth 100% required thus restricting gameplay into a meta-state, tons of bugs still persist (I thought this game was in beta when my friend got it for me, if that tells you anything), and the RNG of items you need was programmed by the biggest dork on the planet.
Suggestions: 1) Get rid of that stupid flashlight. No one will pick that up over glowsticks or a c-foam grenade. It's dead content, bye bye. 2) Make a few enemies spawn in front of you when running to exfil, but more BEHIND you. By the end my average squad HP and ammo is low af, so what we have left should be for a final stand at exfil and not wasted running to it. 3) Oh my god reprogram your AI. They're so, so stupid. The enemy AI is better; that's a problem. "The fodder should never outsmart the farmer." 4) Solo gameplay, even with bots, should be at a lesser difficulty by default but with reduced rewards. Maybe make it so cosmetics can't be acquired unless playing with a team of humans, but with AI it gives mods as rewards. 5) More music to accentuate certain moments or gameplay moments. Music can be immensely immersive yet I can't think of a single piece of music I wanted to hear again throughout my first 9 hours.
I will absolutely be returning to this game frequently. I still recommend it overall. It's been a lot of fun and I can't wait to learn more about the world and story. The challenge is addictive. Good luck, Prisoner.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from game-breaking technical issues such as players being disconnected during missions, sound cutting out entirely, and invisible world geometry.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to like this game. But as it stands right now it's almost impossible to recommend it.

There are elements I find really enjoyable and interesting - but there are so many problems, weird creative decisions, and downright ridiculous elements. Some of which can be fixed or lessened by mods bust mostly not.

Most importantly are the game-breaking bugs:

- After playing for hours on a mostly stealth level and dealing with annoying fog, the game breaks and one of our party is kicked back to the menu, has to re-join and it seemingly breaks the entire level by starting the end-game event. Then 10 minutes later another player has exactly the same problem but can't re-join so the whole run is scrapped.
- Levels in which the sound will just completely stop. For no apparent reason, nothing specific happens to cause it just... stops. For all players. In a game where sound is important that's catastrophic.
- Countless areas in which the world simply becomes invisible. Walking through a doorway only for everything in front to become transparent for a few seconds/steps - particularly helpful for a stealth game.

Then the obnoxious creative decisions:

- Wading through fog you cannot see through, cannot deal with, and which constantly reinfects so that you're essentially playing the rest of the game on 5HP and squinting into nothing trying to feel your way through the levels. 
- The constant alarm on certain levels (R2C2) goes absolutely against everything else the game represents - constantly respawning enemies every 30s is not fun in the slightest and doesn't work for this game. 
- Lighting. I understand the game is supposed to be dark and it's part of the design, but just quite how dark most of the game is doesn't make for a fun experience. Not to mention the diabolical flashlights & glowsticks.
- Spitters on the walls, which can only be temporarily subdued and can be positioned in basically invisible locations. Directly on top of terminals etc.

And the other iss…

the netcode makes the "zombies" invisible, you cannot pickup items , you cannot place turrets.
the game itself is fine, but the netcode breaks the entire experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that stealth, careful resource and ammo management, and tactical planning are required rather than running and gunning.

citations.review_text: very fun and interesting, needs you to actually think and strategise compared to most other shooters where you can run and gun your way through levels

Addictive gameplay loop that becomes ten times better when played with friends.

If you enjoy stealth‑focused tactical gameplay where every decision matters and every mistake can snowball into disaster, this game is exactly what you’re looking for. A tiny slip can cost you dearly, while a smart move can turn into a huge reward. I haven’t found another game that captures this feeling so well, and I’m completely hooked.

Playing with friends elevates the experience even further. We ended up creating our own names for the monsters -> Katusha (the big ones that fire missile bursts), Distance (their smaller, weaker cousins), Prayer (the kneeling melee types), Fatguys (the tanky brutes that can down you in two hits), and so on. Over time, we developed silent takedown routines, communication protocols, and improvised tactics to handle each threat without waking the horde.

A huge part of the game’s depth comes from proper terminal usage. Learning to ping items, list zones, and query resources becomes essential for survival. Efficient terminal work can save entire runs; knowing exactly where medkits, ammo packs, or key objectives are located lets your team plan routes, avoid unnecessary fights, and stay ahead of the chaos. You may even notice you don't need to open certain difficult rooms to progress the mission, sparing meaningful resources.

Ammo is scarce, panic is expensive, and blasting your way out is rarely an option. Learning to stay calm, coordinate, and execute stealthy strategies with your team feels incredibly rewarding.

Good graphics, interesting gameplay, and solid shooting mechanics. The tactical elements are great, you can't just spray and pray because ammo management is tight.

That said, the game isn't perfect. It gets repetitive quickly if you try to play from Rundown 1 to Rundown 8. The lack of enemy variety and the fact that you spend 99% of your time in very similar-looking locations doesn't help either.

Overall a good game, but one that can get boring really fast.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that missions can last several hours without a save and quit feature to pause progress mid-run.

citations.review_text:
Hundreds of hours of fun with friends. The game has some unconventional mechanics in certain missions, go in with an open mind! Just make sure everyone on the team is mature enough to handle the high stakes.

The biggest flaw with this game is that some missions are over 4 hours long, with no way to save and return to it later. You're gonna have to schedule game night!

This game is not for everyone. It's got long ass missions, basically NO way of save and quitting to finish later, and a very difficult skill curve depending on missions. However there is no better feeling than completing an expedition solo with 3 bots after your entire team essentially ceases to exist due to the sheer amount of suffering this game has caused them. 

This game is also one of only two games to have caused my eyes to randomly and spontaneously flash a horde of enemies coming my way. That is not a joke.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the title lacks a progression or rewards system, offering only cosmetics and achievements upon completion.

citations.review_text:
Great game, the difficulty is perfect. It forces teamwork, extremely punishing as described.

It NEEDS DESPERATLY a rewards/progression system. Weapon and tool modifications/unlocks, more cosmetic customization. Add those and it would be perfect. 

Without any sort of progression it lacks motive, the missions take a long dedicated hardcore team of 4 for hours and the only reward you have is the taste of winning and a random cosmetic that looks pretty much the same as anything else.

Hope DOW improves this

And here comes the moment: today we have beaten the game. main, secondary, overload of all levels. I don't even know what to say because by describing it as a journey through hell, getting lost in rundown labyrinths with abominations and having to die again and again and again and again ad-fcking-nauseum is just not doing it justice. it's grit, experience, observation, trial and error, failing better each time so you finally succeed and here we are with a 0.2% rare achievement of this triumphant dopamine spike of telling the game to shove it up its arse by winning--how I want to do the same in life. I like the atmosphere, the enemy types, multiverse references, brutalist architecture, etc. the bots suck but you can fix a lot of the problem with mods. you need at least one very patient friend or acquaintance to play with. it's tactical, stealthy hell, and the horror for me lies in hoping my wifi doesn't go out (it did) at a crucial moment (it did). someone needs to make a "I beat GTFO and all I got was this lousy T-shirt" print, because all you get is just cosmetics in the game and cool colors to your armor....so, give me a tee.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering various technical issues and bugs, including objective items that cannot be interacted with, terminal bugs, and random crashes.

citations.review_text:
There are still a few bugs that remain like glitchy objective item(s) that you can't interact, unable to get ammo, medpack, open doors, random crashes, and others. There are no exclusive in-game setting features like NVIDIA DLSS and Multi-Frame Generation which is kind a suck so that you may able to attain more FPS. Still, this is a decent FPS extraction shooter made in Unity Engine. The graphics? Pretty good I would say. Story? Kind a meh. Continuous support from the developers? Kind of a let down but still, we are hoping that they will fix the remaining bugs. Overall, this game is gorgeously optimized and fun to play especially with random players.

I rate this 7.5 out 10.

Honest Review ig
Negatives first: (Edit; also the server is nearly dead cuz everyone's beaten the game and moved on)

b) sometimes unplayable stuff happens (Liquid bug, Terminal bug, Interact bug)
c) Steep learning curve (Lots of stuff to know if you want to actually play optimally

Positives: 
a) Fun with friends, call ur friends blyats for playing like a pub
b) kinda cool when synchronize

Have a group of friends to play with. or find a group that you can party with often. 
Try to adapt and be more open minded. Many ways you can clear content, not just one (some people wanna clear the level the same way everytime). 
Shooting well is mostly good enough to clear most levels.
"QoL mods" are not needed for the base game, if u r good enough.
Watch a hanimoon guide if stuck. (or Prof Scaler <- the actual normal guide)
Thank h00man for Desync.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking in-game tutorials or explanations for core systems, requiring players to rely on trial and error.

citations.review_text:
It's hard? Yes. It can be unforgiving? Yes. Does it feel rewarding? Hell yeah.
This game isn't for everybody. A lot of stuff isn't explained outright in game and requires some trial and error, but it's no "check the wiki" game.

The game tends to start off rather slow. Just get a bit familiar in a few hours and dare to take risks, and the stealth sections will stop being tedious. Yes, it's a game that gets better as you learn it, but at least it won't take you 10+ hours to get to the fun part.

Finally a co-op FPS game that is actually difficult. I love every aspect of it. Stealth never gets boring, especially once you start to master all the mechanics. And the run and gun moments during alarms make your heart pump. Teamwork is a must, so bring your friends. Otherwise, the official discord server has some awesome people too.

The only real issue with the game is that it doesn't explain much. This could potentially be frustrating for new players as it requires some trial and error before getting the hang of things. Therefore don't hesitate to ask for help. It would be a shame not to play this game because of that.

As for content, this game has plenty of missions, including optional objectives for maximum bragging rights.  Expect needing about 300 hours dedicated to completing all 83 missions. Personally I also like to go the extra mile and play missions truely solo. Because a game can never be hard enough :)
